saveEditor.warningDesc: Before continuing, please read the instructions below carefully. This is not an ordinary feature page — it directly modifies your game save files.
saveEditor.warningCardDesc: Once inside, you can directly modify gold, date, skill levels, mine depth, and villager friendship. These are meant to be earned through normal gameplay, planning, trial and error.
saveEditor.warningP1: Using the save editor essentially bypasses the game's design. You no longer face consequences for seasonal planning mistakes, or need to invest time into gear, money, relationships, or skills. In the short term this accelerates progress dramatically, but the cost is usually not 'less grinding' — it's skipping the core growth process that makes the game meaningful.
saveEditor.warningP2: A large part of Stardew Valley's appeal comes from its rhythm: recovering from a wrong crop, making tradeoffs when money is tight early on, replanning after a bad gift, judging risk in the mines, and looking back at the end of a season to see what you've built. Once you edit values directly, the processes that would have become memorable moments are often reduced to results with no journey.
saveEditor.warningP3: More practically, cheating causes many systems to lose meaning. Set gold too high and the production chain loses pressure; max out skills and early-game tool upgrades, routing, and earning strategies feel hollow; boost friendship directly and gifting, festivals, dialogue, and relationship progression feel like a skipped checklist rather than a story.
saveEditor.warningP4: Save editing also carries real risks beyond experience. Incorrect modifications may cause mismatched values, broken progression, and in severe cases display glitches or confusing game states later on. While this tool automatically backs up the original file, backups only let you roll back — they cannot restore the sense of exploration and growth you've already bypassed.
saveEditor.warningP5: If you're doing this because of a mistake, a bug, a mod conflict, lack of time, or simply not wanting to replay a section, you should at least be clear: this is not a cost-free convenience feature. It can fix results, but it will diminish the game experience, especially on a first playthrough or an actively progressing save.
saveEditor.warningP6: Only continue into the save editor if you fully understand the above consequences and explicitly accept that this will break part — or much — of the game experience.
